statement: The system shall provide real-time drug-drug interaction and allergy contraindication checking at the point of ordering.
stakeholder_statements: S-PRES-02; S-PRES-03; S-PRES-04; S-PRES-05; S-PRES-07; S-PRES-08; S-PHARM-03
acceptance_criteria: The system must display interaction and allergy alerts before the prescriber can sign the order, with a response time of 2 seconds or less for at least 95% of orders.

statement: The system shall provide a patient's active medication list and recorded allergies on the same screen as the order being written.
acceptance_criteria: The patient's active medication list and recorded allergies must be visible on the same screen as the order being written.

statement: The system shall provide interaction and allergy alerts before the prescriber can sign the order, not after it has gone to the pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: Interaction and allergy alerts must appear before the prescriber can sign the order, not after it has been transmitted to the pharmacy.

statement: The system shall provide interaction and allergy alerts that come back within 2 seconds for at least 95% of orders; past 5 seconds prescribers start working around it.
acceptance_criteria: Interaction and allergy alerts must come back within 2 seconds for at least 95% of orders; past 5 seconds prescribers start working around it.

statement: The system shall integrate interaction and allergy alerts handling into a separate project.
acceptance_criteria: Interaction and allergy alerts handling is integrated into a separate project.

statement: NFR-ERX-002: The system shall ensure that quarterly releases after go-live are executed efficiently.
acceptance_criteria: Change control permits quarterly releases after go-live.

statement: The system shall receive prescription details including drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use, and the number of refills authorised when a prescriber requests an e-Rx.
acceptance_criteria: The system receives the required prescription details from the prescriber and verifies that they include the drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use, and the number of refills authorised to ensure the accuracy of the received prescription details.

statement: The system shall verify that every prescription has a drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use and the number of refills authorised before filling the prescription.
acceptance_criteria: The system verifies the presence of a drug name, strength, dose form, quantity, directions for use and the number of refills authorised in the prescription and proceeds to fill the prescription if all details are present.

statement: NFR-ERX-003: The system shall receive e-Rx prescriptions from the hospital EHR network in a format compliant with S-PHARM-14.
acceptance_criteria: The system can receive e-Rx prescriptions from the hospital EHR network in a format compliant with S-PHARM-14.

statement: The system shall send an electronic CancelRx message to the pharmacy when a cancellation occurs, and the prescriber should be able to see the pharmacy's response.
acceptance_criteria: The system can send an electronic CancelRx message to the pharmacy upon cancellation and display the pharmacy’s response to the prescriber.

statement: The system shall display an alert to the prescriber if a drug-drug interaction or allergy is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Prescribers are notified of any detected drug-drug interactions or allergies before issuing prescriptions.

statement: The system shall log and audit any overrides of drug-drug interaction or allergy alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Audit logs capture all instances where prescribers override drug-drug interaction or allergy alerts, including the reason provided.

statement: The system shall generate a report of all alert overrides for the safety committee.
acceptance_criteria: A monthly report detailing all instances where drug-drug interaction or allergy alerts were overridden is produced and reviewed by the safety committee.

statement: The system shall be ONC-certified before the go-live date.
acceptance_criteria: The e-prescribing module is certified by the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC) and meets all required standards.

statement: The system shall maintain an audit trail of all actions related to controlled substance prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system records and retains a detailed log of all actions taken on controlled substance prescriptions, including creation, modification, and deletion.

statement: The system shall analyze the audit trail at least once every calendar day and generate an incident report.
acceptance_criteria: The system reviews the audit trail daily and produces a report identifying any security incidents that could compromise prescription records.

statement: NFR-ERX-007: The system shall be certified against the ONC criteria for CPOE medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checks, and electronic prescribing before go-live.
acceptance_criteria: The system is certified against the ONC criteria for CPOE medications, drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checks, and electronic prescribing.

statement: The system shall retain records for the required period.
acceptance_criteria: Records are retained for the required period as specified by regulatory requirements.

statement: The system shall limit access to a patient's medication data to the patient's care team; any access outside it must be logged and reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: Access to a patient's medication data is limited to the patient's care team, and any access outside this team is logged and reviewed.

statement: The system shall retain audit logs and security documentation for at least 6 years.
acceptance_criteria: Audit logs and security documentation are retained for at least 6 years.

statement: The system shall ensure that every user has a unique account and shared logins are prohibited.
acceptance_criteria: All users must have unique accounts, and shared logins are not allowed.

statement: The system shall encrypt all prescription traffic to the pharmacy intermediary with TLS 1.2 or higher and ensure integrity protection.
acceptance_criteria: All prescription traffic to the pharmacy intermediary is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher and integrity-protected.

statement: The system shall maintain tamper-evident audit records and prevent any application user from deleting them.
acceptance_criteria: Audit records are tamper-evident, and no user can delete them.

statement: The system shall lock sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity and require re-authentication to resume.
acceptance_criteria: Sessions are locked after 15 minutes of inactivity and require re-authentication to resume.

statement: The system shall publish each order as a FHIR R4 MedicationRequest through an adapter, as per S-ARCH-13.
regulations: 45 CFR 170.315(a)(4); 45 CFR 170.315(b)(3); HL7 FHIR R4 MedicationRequest §11.1.3
acceptance_criteria: The system must send each prescription order as a FHIR R4 MedicationRequest via the specified adapter, as per S-ARCH-13.

statement: The system shall be available at least 99.9% per month.
acceptance_criteria: The system must have an uptime of at least 99.9% per month.

statement: The system shall perform real-time drug-drug interaction and patient allergy contraindication checks during the issuance of electronic prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system must perform real-time drug-drug interaction and patient allergy contrindication checks during the issuance of electronic prescriptions.

statement: The system shall perform formulary checks and continue with a 'formulary unavailable' notice if the payer formulary service does not respond within 3 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: If the payer formulary service does not respond within 3 seconds, the system must continue with a 'formulary unavailable' notice.

statement: The system shall eliminate faxed and paper outpatient prescriptions at all four hospitals within 12 months of go-live.
regulations: 45 CFR 170.315(a)(1); 45 CFR 170.315(b)(3); HL7 FHIR R4 MedicationRequest §11.1.3
acceptance_criteria: All four hospitals have no paper or faxed outpatient prescriptions within 12 months of go-live.

statement: The prescriber shall be able to complete a routine prescription in under 90 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Prescribers can complete a routine prescription within 90 seconds.

statement: The system shall enable prescribers to complete a routine prescription for non-controlled medications in under 90 seconds through the EHR interface.
regulations: 45 CFR 170.315(a)(1); 45 CFR 170.315(b)(3); HL7 FHIR R4 MedicationRequest §11.1.3
acceptance_criteria: Prescribers can create, transmit, and receive electronic prescriptions for non-controlled medications through the EHR interface within 90 seconds.

statement: The system shall process the cancellation of electronic prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The prescriber can initiate the cancellation of an issued electronic prescription, and the pharmacy receives a notification of the cancellation.

statement: The system shall provide real-time drug-drug interaction and allergy contraindication checking to support prescribers in completing a routine prescription in under 90 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: The system checks for drug interactions and allergies during the prescription issuance process and alerts the prescriber if any are detected, ensuring that a routine prescription can be completed within 90 seconds.

statement: The system shall provide a reason for every prescription override to the safety committee.
acceptance_criteria: The reason for each prescription override is recorded and visible to the safety committee.

statement: The system shall notify pharmacies of prescription cancellations within 24 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Pharmacies are informed of cancelled prescriptions within 24 hours, preventing the dispensing of incorrect medications.

statement: The system shall transmit electronic prescriptions to community pharmacies through an intermediary.
regulations: 45 CFR 170.315(a)(1); 45 CFR 170.315(b)(3); HL7 FHIR R4 MedicationRequest §11.1.3
acceptance_criteria: The system can transmit electronic prescriptions to community pharmacies via the existing e-prescribing intermediary.

statement: The system shall conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI related to electronic prescription issuance.
acceptance_criteria: The risk assessment report must be reviewed and approved by the compliance officer, documenting identified risks and proposed mitigation strategies.

statement: The system shall allow access to systems that maintain ePHI only to persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.
acceptance_criteria: Access logs must show that only authorized personnel and software programs have accessed the ePHI related to electronic prescriptions.

statement: The system shall establish procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
acceptance_criteria: Emergency procedures must be documented and include steps for accessing ePHI in a crisis situation.

statement: The system shall protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction.
acceptance_criteria: Data integrity checks must be performed on ePHI related to electronic prescriptions, and any changes must be logged and auditable.

statement: The system shall verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
acceptance_criteria: Authentication mechanisms must be in place for verifying the identity of users accessing ePHI related to electronic prescriptions.

statement: The system shall guard against unauthorized access to ePHI being transmitted over an electronic communications network; integrity controls and encryption are addressable.
acceptance_criteria: Encryption must be implemented for data in transit, and integrity controls must be in place to ensure the accuracy of transmitted ePHI related to electronic prescriptions.

statement: The system shall encrypt electronic health information stored on end-user devices after use stops, or prevent it from being stored locally.
acceptance_criteria: All electronic health information stored on end-user devices must be encrypted using a recognized encryption standard and the encryption must be applied immediately upon cessation of use or before data is stored locally.
